attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6's strongest new idea, and it is a correction to the naive reading of continuity rather than an addition to it. An inherited `xor.cuda` that will not run on a CPU-only host is NOT a continuity violation: its guarantee was conditional on a CUDA runtime, the assumption is undischarged, and the continuity claim was `assume A, guarantee G` throughout. The violation is reporting it available. Registered as ASM-CAPABILITY-CONTRACT and consumed by five `contract_relative` cells in mosaic/operations.json, each of which must name what the system reports when the contract fails — check-mosaic.mjs §10 refuses a `contract_relative` cell without an `unavailable_report`, because that report is the entire content of the kind.
attrs.prior_art: Assume-guarantee reasoning. The nearest neighbour already in this ledger is the Simplex architecture work (Phan et al., arXiv 1704.04759). Within this portfolio it is the same distinction as STALE ≠ UNESTABLISHED.
attrs.review_focus: DEF-R7-CONTRACT-UNPOPULATED is open against it: no capability contract is written anywhere, because the Contract Registry GPT-5.6 lists as existing does not exist and the assumption slot standing in for it holds four records.
attrs.statement: An inherited capability is part of the successor's effective embodiment exactly while its contract assumptions remain discharged; when they do not, the system must report it UNAVAILABLE rather than present it as available.
